title: The Dooars on a Budget: What Things Really Cost
meta_description: Real 2025–26 Dooars prices for safari jeeps, homestays, forest lodges, trains and buses, with two daily budgets and the places people overspend.
summary: The Dooars cost about ₹1,800–2,500 a person a day on a shoestring and ₹2,500–4,000 at a comfortable value level, if you share safari jeeps, sleep in homestays and ride the Dooars line trains between bases. Reserved cars for every hop and unshared jeeps are what push budgets up. Here are indicative 2025–26 prices.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: The Dooars are one of the cheapest wildlife regions in India, cheaper than Kaziranga, far cheaper than the tiger parks of central India, and closer to a railhead than either. A family homestay in Lataguri, Buxa or Jayanti charges ₹1,200–2,000 a person with dinner and breakfast. A safari jeep for up to six people, with entry, guide and vehicle fees, costs ₹2,500–4,000, so a full jeep brings your share down to ₹450–700. Trains on the Dooars line from NJP to Malbazar, Madarihat or Alipurduar cost less than a plate of biryani in Siliguri.

What breaks budgets here is not the forest. It is the car hired for the whole trip when it sits idle for two days, the jeep booked for two people when four seats stayed empty, and the resort in Lataguri at ₹5,000 a night for a room you only sleep in between a 6 am safari and a 3 pm one. The prices below are indicative for 2025–26. Safari fees, jeep rates and forest lodge tariffs are revised often, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: A price list for 2025–26
paras: These are the figures we use when we plan Dooars trips for friends. Rooms are per night; everything else is per person unless marked. Winter weekends, Christmas week and the Durga Puja holidays in October push private room prices up, and the forest corporation lodges fill first.

sections.heading: Two day budgets that work
paras: A shoestring day assumes a homestay with meals, one shared safari seat, a train or bus to the next base every second day, a dhaba lunch and tea from stalls. A value day assumes a forest corporation cottage or a clean small hotel, a private jeep split between two or three people, a local car for short transfers and a sit-down dinner. Both figures are per person with two people sharing a room.
list: Shoestring: homestay with meals ₹1,400 + shared safari seat ₹550 + train or bus averaged ₹100 + lunch and tea ₹250 = about ₹2,300
Value: forest corporation room share ₹1,500 + camp meals ₹600 + half a private jeep ₹1,500 + local car share ₹500 + snacks ₹200 = about ₹4,300
Trekking day at Buxa or Jayanti: homestay with meals ₹1,500 + guide share ₹400 + forest fees ₹150 + tea ₹100 = about ₹2,150

sections.heading: Where the money really goes
paras: Safaris are the largest single cost, and the fees are per vehicle, not per person. The jeep, the driver, the compulsory forest guide, the vehicle entry fee and the per-person entry fee are added together, so two people paying for an empty six-seat jeep can spend three times what a full jeep costs each. Homestay hosts in Lataguri and Madarihat often know other guests who want to share. Ask the night before; many will make the booking for you if you give them your ID details.

The second cost is transport between bases. Gorumara, Jaldapara and Buxa sit in a line about 60–80 km apart along the foothills, and the Dooars line railway follows the same line. A car from Lataguri to Madarihat costs ₹3,000–3,500; the train from New Mal Junction or Chalsa to Madarihat costs a fraction of that and takes about two hours. You need a local car or an auto at each end, usually ₹300–800.

The third cost is the room. Lataguri's highway resorts charge ₹3,000–6,000 for rooms with televisions and swimming pools that you will barely see. Forest corporation cottages at Murti, Suntalekhola, Jhalong and Mendabari cost less, sit inside or beside the forest, and include the sound of the river at night.

sections.heading: Six ways we save money here
paras: None of these mean a worse trip. Most of them put you closer to the forest and the people who live beside it.
list: Book safari slots online as soon as dates are fixed, and fill the jeep: six people in one vehicle cost each person a sixth of the fees.
Use the Dooars line train between Gorumara and Jaldapara instead of a reserved car, and hire short local rides at each station.
Stay in a homestay that cooks for you; lodge restaurants and resort dining rooms charge two to three times a dhaba price.
Travel on weekdays: forest lodge rooms and safari slots for Friday to Sunday sell out first, and some private rooms cost more.
Choose one park per base and stay two nights, so you can take an evening and a morning safari without paying for a transfer in between.
Carry cash in small notes: ATMs exist in Malbazar, Birpara, Madarihat and Alipurduar, but forest villages such as Buxa, Jayanti and Bindu have none.

sections.heading: Base by base: what changes
paras: Costs are not the same across the Dooars, and it helps to know where your money stretches furthest.

Lataguri is the most crowded and the most competitive. Dozens of homestays and resorts line the highway, so prices are fair in the cheap range and inflated at the top. Food is easy: dhabas on the main road serve fish thalis for ₹150–300. Murti, 15 minutes away, has fewer rooms, mostly the forest corporation's riverside cottages and a few private resorts, and you will eat where you sleep.

Madarihat, the base for Jaldapara, is a small market town with budget hotels at ₹1,500–2,500 a room, a WBTDC tourist lodge and cheap dhabas near the bus stand. It is also on the railway, which keeps transport costs down. Chilapata, 20–30 minutes east, has only forest corporation rooms and adds a car fare each way.

Buxa and Jayanti are the cheapest bases of all once you are there: simple homestays, ₹100–200 forest fees and walks that cost nothing but a guide's day rate. The cost is getting there, since both lie beyond Alipurduar, five hours from NJP. Samsing, Suntalekhola, Jhalong and Bindu sit up side valleys where shared jeeps run mostly in the morning; miss them and a local car costs ₹800–2,000.

sections.heading: What a whole trip costs
paras: A four-night trip from NJP covering Gorumara and Jaldapara, with homestays, shared safaris and trains, costs about ₹9,000–11,000 per person. The same trip with forest corporation cottages, private jeeps shared between two and a car for the first and last legs comes to about ₹13,000–15,000. A seven-night trip that adds Samsing or Jhalong and the walk to Buxa Fort adds roughly ₹2,000 per person per night on a shoestring and ₹3,500 at a value level.

Foreign nationals pay higher park entry and camera fees, and the difference is significant on a trip with four or five safaris. Students should carry a college ID: some forest counters have offered concessions, though rules vary by park. Prices quoted to you by agents usually include a margin of ₹300–800 a safari, which may be worth it on a holiday weekend when the online slots are gone. Fees and fares change each season; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does a Dooars trip cost per day?
faqs.a: About ₹1,800–2,500 per person a day on a shoestring, with a homestay including meals, a shared safari seat and trains or buses between bases. A value trip with forest corporation cottages and private jeeps shared between two costs ₹2,500–4,000. Resorts and a car for the whole trip push it to ₹4,000–6,500. These are indicative 2025–26 figures.

faqs.q: How much is a Gorumara safari?
faqs.a: A watchtower safari for a jeep of up to six, including entry, guide and vehicle fees, costs roughly ₹2,500–3,500, so a full jeep works out at ₹450–600 a person. Video camera fees are extra. Rates are revised by the forest department, so check current status before you travel and book online when you can.

faqs.q: How much does a Jaldapara jeep safari cost?
faqs.a: About ₹2,500–4,000 for a six-seat jeep with fees in 2025–26, depending on the route and slot. Elephant safaris, when the forest department runs them, have cost about ₹800–1,000 per Indian national. Foreign nationals pay more. Book online early, because morning slots sell out on winter weekends.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to travel by train in the Dooars?
faqs.a: Yes, by a wide margin. Dooars line trains from NJP to New Mal Junction, Chalsa, Madarihat, Hasimara and Alipurduar cost ₹40–450 depending on class, while a reserved car on the same routes costs ₹3,000–5,000. You still need a local car or auto at each end. Timetables change, so check before you plan.

faqs.q: What does a homestay cost in Lataguri or Buxa?
faqs.a: Usually ₹1,200–2,000 per person a night with dinner and breakfast, and sometimes lunch for a little more. Prices are higher around Christmas, New Year and the Durga Puja holidays. Homestays in Buxa and Jayanti are simpler than those on the Lataguri highway, with shared bathrooms in some houses, and cost toward the lower end.

faqs.q: Can we share a safari jeep with strangers?
faqs.a: Yes, and most budget travellers do. Fees are charged per vehicle plus per person, so filling a six-seat jeep cuts each share sharply. Homestay hosts and jeep drivers in Lataguri and Madarihat often pair groups. Every passenger's ID details may be needed for the booking, so agree on the group before the slot is booked.

faqs.q: Are there ATMs in the Dooars?
faqs.a: In the towns, yes: Malbazar, Chalsa, Birpara, Madarihat, Hasimara and Alipurduar have ATMs, and UPI works in most shops on the highway. Forest villages such as Buxa, Jayanti, Bindu and Suntalekhola have no ATM and patchy mobile data, so carry enough cash in small notes for homestays, guides and tea.

faqs.q: Do foreigners pay more for Dooars safaris?
faqs.a: Yes. Foreign nationals pay higher entry and camera fees at Gorumara, Jaldapara, Chapramari and Buxa, and the difference adds up over several safaris. Carry your passport, as IDs are checked against the booking. Budget roughly a third to a half more for safaris than an Indian traveller would, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is a four-night Dooars trip possible on ₹10,000?
faqs.a: Yes, on a shoestring. Take the train from NJP to New Mal Junction, stay two nights in a Lataguri homestay for Gorumara, take the train on to Madarihat for two nights and Jaldapara, and share every safari jeep. Expect to spend ₹9,000–11,000 per person including meals, safaris and transport from and back to NJP.
